newsitem.title: UK: Right-wing UK MP apologises for slur on minister.
newsitem.headline: Right-wing UK MP apologises for slur on minister.

text.p: British cabinet minister Virginia Bottomley said on Wednesday that an outspoken fellow Conservative who had described her as "dead from the neck upwards" had apologised for the slur.

But David Evans, a colourful right-winger, further embarrassed the ruling party by heaping abuse on the main opposition Labour party's female candidate, who is trying to unseat him at a coming general election.
Labour is hot favourite to oust the Conservatives from power at polls expected on May 1.

In an interview at a local school that he thought was confidential, Evans said Melanie Johnson, Labour's contender for Evans's constituency, had "never done a proper job" and was the mother of "three bastard children".

Evans, a self-made millionaire, went on to describe Prime Minister John Major as "vindictive and not forgiving" and used the phrase "black bastard" when discussing crime. The transcript of his interview was given to a regional television station.
Although Evans is not influential within the ruling party, his outburst ensured the already politically beleaguered Major another day of negative headlines in Britain's daily newspapers.
"Big mouth puts his foot in it," the pro-Conservative Daily Mail said of Evans on its front page.
Labour said the crude remarks showed Evans was not fit to be a member of parliament.
But Bottomley, the national heritage secretary, tried to make light of the row.
"I have had a very gallant and elegant apology from him, which is much appreciated," she told BBC radio.
Labour's Johnson, who is a full-time schools inspector and magistrate has three children by the man with whom she has lived for 18 years, said she was appalled by Evans's outburst.
"I don't think these kind of comments go down well," she told the BBC. "I think it does show he must be pretty desperate."
